subject: SOC 2 Type II coverage for multi-mode deployment & architecture ownership
messages:
From: Jordan Hayes <security@acmefin.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmefin.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — scope for Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC

Hi Kimberly,

Quick one from our audit team as we prepare procurement docs: Acme needs confirmation whether Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report and any bridge letters cover customer workloads hosted in three distinct modes — (1) Redwood Hosted (multi-tenant), (2) Dedicated GPU pools (Redwood-managed, tenant isolated), and (3) Private/VPC/on-prem deployments where the customer manages networking.

Specifically:
- Which modes are explicitly in-scope for the attached template wording?
- For Dedicated pools, do you consider customer tenants "in-scope" for the same controls as Hosted, or is there an evidence gap?
- For Private/VPC, can you provide the audit ownership split we should present to our auditor (Redwood responsibilities vs Acme responsibilities)?

We'd like any supporting artifacts you can share (architecture diagram, proposed bridge letter language, control ownership matrix). Our Type II review window is Jul 1 — Sep 30, so clarifying now will help the audit plan.

Thanks — Jordan
Security Manager
Acme Financial

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <security@acmefin.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — scope for Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Short answer up front: our Type II report covers Redwood-managed control implementation for Hosted and Dedicated deployment modes; Private/VPC/on-prem is treated as a customer-controlled environment for certain controls and requires a split-ownership matrix plus a short bridge letter where applicable.

Notes and next steps:
- Hosted (multi-tenant): fully in-scope for Redwood controls in the report; evidence available (control narratives, testing results).
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed pools): considered in-scope provided the workload runs on Redwood-managed instances and we are responsible for the control implementations (networking, hypervisor access, operational patching). There are a few tenant-bound controls where sampling differs — we can supply sampling approach and a tenant mapping.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: Redwood is responsible for our agent/runtime and any managed services; customer is responsible for network controls, physical controls, and cloud account configuration. We'll provide a clear control ownership matrix and suggested language for the auditor.

I'll attach an architecture diagram and a draft bridge letter for your audit team. Priya, can you add the hosting-boundary matrix and call out any controls that commonly require auditor acceptance? Ben — heads-up: Procurement may want to reference this in the contract SOW.

Deliverables we will share by next Tue: architecture diagram, hosting-boundary matrix (xlsx), draft bridge letter (PDF). If your auditor prefers a formal bridge letter template with signatures, tell me and we'll route through legal.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: redwood-architecture-diagram-v2.pdf (diagram), hosting-boundary-matrix.xlsx (control ownership), soc2-typeii-bridgeletter-draft.pdf (draft)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Hayes <security@acmefin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — scope for Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC

Jordan / Kimberly — attaching the hosting-boundary matrix here (see summary rows). Quick highlights:
- Controls exclusively Redwood-managed: physical security of our data centers (hosted), key management in-hosted service, runtime patching for Redwood-managed GPUs (hosted & dedicated).
- Controls with shared responsibility: logical access (we enforce service-side IAM; customers manage tenant admin accounts), network segmentation (Redwood enforces intra-cluster segmentation; customer controls VPC perimeter).
- Typical auditor questions: sampling of Dedicated pools (we provide tenant mapping + sampling rationale), evidence for backfill if audit period predates a Dedicated pool onboarding.

If Acme wants the bridge letter to state that Dedicated pools are "audited in-scope subject to tenant mapping and sampling" we can include that phrasing; otherwise auditors often prefer explicit control lists with owner tags.

Priya Natarajan
Security & Compliance Lead — Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: hosting-boundary-matrix.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Hayes <security@acmefin.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — scope for Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC

Jordan — thanks for working with us on this. Confirming receipt of the diagram, matrix, and draft bridge letter. Action items for procurement:
- If Acme needs the bridge letter with an executed signature, we can route the final version through Legal and provide an executed PDF.
- For the audit plan: please add Redwood as "service provider" in your auditor intake and share the auditor contact; we'll coordinate a short control walkthrough call (30 min) focusing on Dedicated sampling and ownership for Private/VPC setups.

I'll leave scheduling to your procurement team; Kimberly & Priya will maintain the evidence pack.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments included in final mail: redwood-architecture-diagram-v2.pdf, hosting-boundary-matrix.xlsx, soc2-typeii-bridgeletter-draft.pdf
